complexity: O(pages) requests to list all items
data_flow_ascii:
APIClient.list_all -> request per page -> FakeAPI.handle
simulated 500 -> sleep backoff -> retry (up to max_retries)
200 responses -> combined item list + full request history printed
description_sentence: A simulated REST API client that paginates through an in-process fake API, retrying simulated server errors with backoff.
failure_note: Simulated 500s are retried up to max_retries, then APIError is raised with status and body; 404s fail fast with no retry.

label: API client sim
output_shape: Prints the fetched item table, a single-item fetch, and the full request history showing retries after simulated 500s.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that pages through results and automatically retries failed requests, and I proved it against a simulated flaky server.

qa.a: The first fail_first handle() calls return 500 regardless of path, so the client must retry before any data flows.
Only 500s are retried, with a 0.01s * attempt linear backoff; 404s raise APIError immediately.
list_all keeps requesting page N+1 until the accumulated items reach the total reported by the API.
qa.q: How does pagination know when to stop?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with paginated fetching, retry-on-500 with backoff, and a full request history for debugging.
run_notes: --per-page and --max-retries tune the demo; item count and simulated failures come from @@TOPIC_PARAMS@@.
scaling_note: In-process fake: no real HTTP, connection pooling, or TLS; the client logic is what is being demonstrated.
storage_note: In-memory only: the fake dataset and request history vanish when the process exits.
tradeoff_note: A fake in-process API keeps the demo hermetic and fast, at the cost of not exercising real network behavior.
